english_classification.chapter_title: A Catechumen asked the Apostle: When I would give an Offering to the Saints, shall I inflict a Wound on the Alms?
english_classification.chapter_note: This chapter is entirely institutional/pastoral. It addresses a practical concern of Manichaean community life — the catechumen's worry about harming the living soul while preparing alms-offerings for the elect. The teaching response uses a general human analogy (an enemy who strikes vs. a doctor who cuts to heal) to reassure the questioner. No cosmological-correspondential substrate is present: there are no cosmic-domain-to-cosmic-domain mappings, no systematic nomenclature, no zoomorphic/metal/taste correspondences. The concept of the 'living soul' bound in matter is presupposed as background knowledge, not expounded as teaching. Teaching purity score (0.132) confirms almost no substrate vocabulary. The entire chapter entered the text as institutional composition — a catechetical dialogue about community alms practice.
